item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 2, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, President of the Gabonese Republic Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema will pay a state visit to China from November 3 to 7. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi and Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao will co-chair the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting via video conference in Beijing on November 3. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will chair the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Beijing from November 3 to 4. Xinhua News Agency: To follow up on your announcement about Gabon’s President Nguema’s upcoming visit to China, can you share the arrangements and China’s expectation of the visit? How does China view its relations with Gabon? Mao Ning: This will be President Nguema’s first state visit to China since he took office. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold a welcome ceremony and a welcome banquet for President Nguema. The two heads of state will hold talks. Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him respectively. President Nguema will also attend the ninth China International Import Expo and visit Shanghai. China and Gabon are comprehensive strategic cooperative partners that enjoy traditional friendship and mutual trust. Over the past 52 years of diplomatic relations, the two countries have supported and helped each other, engaged in fruitful practical cooperation in various fields, and had close coordination and collaboration on multilateral affairs. Through the visit, China stands ready to work with Gabon to elevate bilateral relations to a new height and make greater contribution to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. Yonhap News Agency: It’s reported that the DPRK on October 31 announced that it conducted a test of a cluster warhead for tactical ballistic missile. The test violates UN Security Council resolutions concerning the DPRK, and comes at a time when the ROK has proposed military talks, which the DPRK has yet to respond. What’s China’s comment on the DPRK’s test launch? Mao Ning: China noted the relevant report and the fact that the DPRK has recently expressed its position on multiple occasions regarding the military activities by the U.S., the ROK and Japan. We hope the relevant parties will face up to the root cause of the Korean Peninsula issue, stick to the direction of political settlement, and make efforts to ease tensions and maintain peace and stability in the region. Yonhap News Agency: The FBI said on October 31 that the DPRK was behind the hacking of Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in which about US$ 6.3 billion was stolen. U.S. President Trump said he would discuss the matter with the DPRK if the allegations are confirmed. What is China’s view on this incident and President Trump’s related remarks? Mao Ning: We are not familiar with that. CGTN: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin just concluded their visits to China. How does China assess the outcomes of the two visits? What’s China’s expectation of China-Germany relations and China-Switzerland relations moving forward? Mao Ning: This is President Steinmeier’s first state visit to China in eight years, and the first visit by a Swiss president to China in seven years. President Xi Jinping held talks with President Steinmeier and met with President Parmelin. President Xi and President Steinmeier noted that as the world’s second and third largest economies, China and Germany should shoulder the responsibility for safeguarding world peace and development and striving for a more just and equitable global governance system. Both sides spoke highly of the fruitful outcomes of China-Germany relations, and agreed to uphold mutual respect and equality, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen people-to-people exchanges, and properly handle differences through dialogue and consultation, so as to usher in a new chapter of China-Germany all-round strategic partnership. President Xi and President Parmelin agreed to respect each other’s core interests, consolidate political mutual trust, make good use of the dialogue mechanisms in various fields, deepen collaboration on bilateral and multilateral affairs, champion multilateralism and free trade, and elevate China-Switzerland relations to a new height. The two presidents witnessed the signing of the Protocol Enhancing the Free Trade Agreement between China and Switzerland and other cooperation documents, including on scientific research, labor and employment, and media. Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and the dimension of change and turbulence is becoming more prominent. The two presidents’ visits to China have sent out a positive message of strengthening communication and coordination, deepening open cooperation, and supporting multilateralism and free trade, and set a sound example for the growth of China-EU relations. China will work with various parities to focus on cooperation and mutual benefits, and inject more certainty to the stability and prosperity in today’s world. Shenzhen TV: Could you share the background of the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting? As the host, what are China’s expectations for the event? Mao Ning: This year marks the 10th anniversary of the first LMC Leaders’ Meeting. Over the past decade, with the concerted efforts of all countries, LMC has grown from strength to strength, becoming a stellar example of regional cooperation brimming with vitality and potential. Solid progress has been made in building a community with a shared future between China and the five Mekong countries bilaterally and multilaterally. Trade between the two sides has exceeded US$500 billion, up by 150 percent compared with that of 10 years ago. Efforts in building the LMC Economic Development Belt have yielded fruitful outcomes. The Lancang-Mekong Innovation Corridor has become a new highlight. Faster headway is being made in boosting regional power connectivity. The LMC Special Fund has provided support for over 1,000 small and smart projects. The Lancang-Mekong Sweet Spring Action and the Hundred, Thousand, Ten Thousand Action Plan on Lancang-Mekong Agricultural Cooperation, among others, have delivered real results. The Lancang-Mekong Visa has facilitated people-to-people exchanges among the six countries. As the century-defining transformation unfolds at an accelerating pace, LMC’s role in promoting openness and development and safeguarding peace and tranquility is becoming even more pronounced. China hopes to take the upcoming Foreign Ministers’ Meeting as an opportunity to work with the five Mekong countries to take stock of past experience, plan future cooperation, discuss in particular the blueprint for LMC 2.0, explore new mechanisms for openness and cooperation, build more platforms for industrial innovation, and make greater progress in law enforcement and security cooperation, so as to inject strong impetus into building a Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future of peace, prosperity and sustainable development. People’s Daily: On October 31 Beijing time, the Committee on Disarmament and International Security (First Committee) of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly adopted the resolution “Promoting international cooperation on peaceful uses in the context of international security” tabled by China. Could you share more details? Mao Ning: We welcome the adoption by the First Committee of the resolution “Promoting international cooperation on peaceful uses in the context of international security.” The resolution calls for efforts to coordinate both development and security, strengthen the role of the UN, and safeguard developing countries’ lawful rights to peaceful uses of technology. The resolution urges all countries to take concrete actions to promote international cooperation on peaceful uses, and avoid maintaining restrictions incompatible with their international obligations. The resolution also decides to continue consideration of the relevant issue at the UN General Assembly. This is the fourth time for China to submit the resolution on peaceful uses of technology to the UN General Assembly since 2021, which has received broad support from the international community. Acting on the resolution is an important step for China to implement the Global Security Initiative. We will work with various parties to promote the full and effective implementation of the resolution and make sure that progress in technology will further contribute to peace and development for humanity. Global Times: The Spokesperson said a few days ago that China will send special envoys to the Middle East, the Gulf region, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. Can you share more details? Mao Ning: To deliver on the initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on promoting peace and security in the Middle East and the four principles on the constructive participation of relevant parties in the resolution of African hotspot issues, Special Envoy of the Chinese Government on the Middle East Issue Zhai Jun will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early and mid-November; Special Representative of the Chinese Government on African Affairs Liu Xianfa will visit Ethiopia, Djibouti and Egypt in early and mid-November; and Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Affairs of the Foreign Ministry Hu Changchun will visit Eritrea in early November. These shuttle diplomacy visits in this period of time by Chinese special envoys and special representative are aimed at promoting peace talks, easing tensions, and playing a constructive role for upholding regional peace and stability.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 30, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
At the invitation of the government of the Republic of Senegal, President Xi Jinping’s Special Envoy and Director of China’s General Administration of Sport Gao Zhidan will attend the opening ceremony of the fourth Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal on October 31. At the invitation of Premier of the State Council Li Qiang, Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker of Austria will pay an official visit to China from November 2 to 7. CCTV: The Chinese side has announced that Sultan Haitham of Oman will pay a state visit to China. Could you share the program of the visit? How does China view the current state of bilateral relations? What are your expectations for the visit? Guo Jiakun: This will be the first visit to China by Sultan Haitham since ascending to the throne and by an Omani head of state since diplomatic ties were established 48 years ago. As such, it is of great significance for advancing bilateral relations. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with Sultan Haitham to have an in-depth exchange of view on China-Oman relations and issues of mutual interest. There will also be a meeting with Premier Li Qiang. China and Oman enjoy a profound traditional friendship. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi and Sultan Haitham, our two countries have seen deepening political mutual trust, steady progress in mutually beneficial cooperation, increasingly close people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and good communication in international and regional issues. We hope to work together with the Omani side to take the upcoming visit as an opportunity to bring our strategic partnership to new heights. China News Service: We notice that the Committee on Disarmament and International Security (First Committee) of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly approved resolutions on “Further practical measures for the prevention of an arms race in outer space” and “No first placement of weapons in outer space.” The vision of a community with a shared future for humanity was again included in the resolutions. Could you share more details? Guo Jiakun: China advocates the peaceful use and safety of outer space, and promotes the building of a community with a shared future for humanity in the domain of outer space. Since 2017, China has, together with relevant countries, jointly submitted to the First Committee of the UN General Assembly each year the two resolutions on “Further practical measures for the prevention of an arms race in outer space” and “No first placement of weapons in outer space.” China firmly opposes the weaponization of and any arms race in outer space, and calls for negotiations on an international legal instrument to safeguard lasting peace and common security and build a community with a shared future for humanity in the domain of outer space. The First Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly once again adopted the above resolutions by a majority. This marks the tenth consecutive year that the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity has been incorporated into UNGA resolutions on outer space. It fully demonstrates that the vision conforms to the trend of the times and meets the common expectations of the international community, and has become an international public good of major significance in today’s world. The recently released China’s Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance is consistent with this vision. China stands ready to work with the international community to jointly build a peaceful, secure, open and cooperative outer space, and to ensure that the outcomes of outer space exploration benefit all humanity. AFP: The New York Times had an exclusive report about how a Chinese businesswoman, who was close to NVIDIA Chief Jensen Huang, was found to be giving intelligence to Beijing. This is according to intelligence from American spy agencies. Is China aware of this report, and do you have a comment on this? Guo Jiakun: Relevant report is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China. People’s Daily: China just announced the upcoming visit of Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker. Could you please share more information about the program? How does China see the current China-Austria relations and what’s China’s expectation for the visit? Guo Jiakun: This will be Chancellor Stocker’s first visit to China since taking office, and the first visit by an Austrian chancellor to China in seven years. Chancellor Stocker will first land in Shanghai, where he will attend the ninth China International Import Expo. During his stay in Beijing, President Xi Jinping will meet with Chancellor Stocker, and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will hold talks and meet with him respectively. Austria is a friendly strategic partner of China in Europe. This year marks the 55th anniversary of our diplomatic relations. At present, the two countries enjoy sound momentum of growth in bilateral ties, with close high-level interactions and ever-deepening exchanges and cooperation in various fields. As the two countries mark the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations, China stands ready to work with Austria to deepen political mutual trust, strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation and carry forward our traditional friendship based on mutual respect and equality, so as to deliver more practical outcomes in bilateral ties and help stabilize and improve China-Europe economic and trade relations at an early date. CCTV: The G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting will be held in Atlanta, the U.S. South Africa, a founding member of the G20, was once again not invited. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: As a major platform for international economic cooperation, the G20 plays an important role in strengthening multilateralism, promoting world economic growth, and improving global governance. South Africa is an important member of the G20. China supports South Africa in continuing its participation in G20 activities. AFP: The Swiss President Guy Parmelin will meet with President Xi Jinping. Following the meeting, both countries will sign an optimized bilateral free trade agreement. Can China share the expectations you have for this upgraded agreement? Guo Jiakun: We’ve shared information on President Parmelin’s visit to China. There will be timely updates on the visit. Please stay tuned. Reuters: We had a story out of Washington that U.S. telecom regulator is voting next month to ban Chinese telecom companies from direct access to U.S. telephone numbers. And also the same U.S. regulator has decided to ban all Chinese labs from testing U.S. electronics like smartphones. Any comment regarding those matters? Guo Jiakun: The U.S. is overstretching the concept of national security and abusing state power to go after Chinese businesses. China firmly opposes and deplores this. The U.S. move severely hinders normal economic and trade cooperation between Chinese and American businesses and is not in the interest of any party including US companies and consumers. China will do what is necessary to firmly defend its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 29, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
CGTN: On October 28 local time, the 81st UN General Assembly adopted the draft resolution titled “Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba.” What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The illegal economic embargo and unilateral economic sanctions imposed by the U.S. against Cuba have lasted for 64 years, inflicting untold suffering on Cuban people. Since 1992, the UN General Assembly has voted overwhelmingly to adopt the resolution calling for an end to U.S.’s economic, commercial and financial embargo against Cuba for 34 consecutive times. It shows that the overwhelming majority of countries in the world are outraged by the U.S.’s serious violation of the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and underscores the international community’s longstanding call for the U.S. to immediately stop infringing on Cuban people’s right to survive and thrive. China will continue firmly supporting Cuba’s just effort for safeguarding national sovereignty and dignity, and opposing external interference and embargo. We once again urge the U.S. to heed the call for justice from the international community, immediately lift its blockade and sanctions against Cuba, and stop all forms of coercion and pressure on Cuba, including through the threat of force. China-Arab TV: Pakistani Defence Minister said yesterday that Pakistan has closed its airspace to airlines of China’s Taiwan region in adherence to the one-China policy. This makes Pakistan the first country in the world to take such a measure. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: The one-China principle is a prevailing consensus of the international community. To our knowledge, there is no impediment to the international travel by residents of the Taiwan region. Associated Press: The U.S. announced a ban to imports from three Chinese biotechnology companies. I know that the Ministry of Commerce already condemned the decision, but I want to hear from MOFA if you think that this decision will affect the upcoming meeting between Chinese and U.S. presidents? Guo Jiakun: The U.S. has been spreading disinformation about Xinjiang and using so-called “forced labor” as false pretext to suppress Chinese enterprises. China deplores and firmly opposes the move. The so-called “forced labor” is a huge lie propagated by anti-China forces to destabilize Xinjiang, smear China and curb its development. China urges the U.S. to stop interfering in China’s internal affairs and curbing China’s development in the name of human rights. China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard the lawful rights and interests of Chinese enterprises. Yonhap News Agency: The DPRK fired more than ten short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on October 29, a move in violation of relevant UN Security Council resolutions. What is China’s comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We noted that relevant parties have different views on what the projectiles are. We hope relevant parties will face up to the root cause of the Korean Peninsula issue, stick to the direction of political settlement, and make an effort for peace and stability in the region. Associated Press: Today, there’s an ASEAN meeting in the Philippines. The U.S. and Japan announced an agreement to jointly produce advanced air-to-air missiles in Japan. What is the comment from China? Guo Jiakun: The development of bilateral relations and security cooperation between the U.S. and Japan should not come at the price of regional peace and stability, nor should such developments target or harm the interests of any third country. Since the current administration came to power, it has been breaking free from the constraints of the international and domestic laws in the name of coping with the so-called “threats,” which constitutes a challenge to the postwar international order and a threat to regional peace and stability. The international community must stay on high alert and firmly reject such moves. AFP: Australia’s Defense Minister said Thursday that China’s military buildup was creating a “condition of pressure” in Southeast Asia, and said we are “obviously seeing the biggest conventional military buildup that the world has seen since the end of the second World War from China.” Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this? Guo Jiakun: China is committed to the path of peaceful development. The development of military capabilities aims to safeguard national sovereignty, security and development interests. We never target any country nor seek military expansion. The relevant party should view this objectively and stop making irresponsible comments. Reuters: The Japanese toy company Sanrio has canceled a partnership with a Japanese spy drama because of the social media backlash in China. Does China have any response? Guo Jiakun: We have noted relevant reports. This TV drama once again shows that there is a force in Japan continuously seeking to use cultural products to vilify and smear China and disseminate hatred against China. The international community and insightful people in Japan must be vigilant against this.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 28, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
CCTV: China just announced that President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin will visit China. How does China view its relations with Switzerland? What’s China’s expectation of this visit? Guo Jiakun: We welcome President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin to visit China. President Xi Jinping will meet with him. This year marks the 10th anniversary of China-Switzerland innovative strategic partnership. At present, China-Switzerland relations maintain sound growth momentum, with fruitful cooperation in various areas. In particular, our cooperation on free trade has become the biggest highlight of the bilateral ties. Switzerland is the first country on the European continent to sign a free trade agreement with China. Since its entry into effect over a decade ago, the agreement has greatly facilitated the business exchanges between the two countries. In August this year, Switzerland became the first European country to complete the negotiations on an upgrade of the free trade agreement with China. China will work with Switzerland to bring more benefits to our two peoples, more convenience to our business communities, and more certainty to the growth of world economy through stable China-Switzerland relations. Reuters: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has called on European and Asian middle powers to build a strategic alliance in trade, technology and security in his speech in Singapore yesterday. And even though he warned that a full economic decoupling from China would be “a mistake,” he said that Europe and Asia must reduce “unhealthy, one-sided dependencies.” On Germany’s policy towards China, he described it as “coming of age” and aligned with the EU. On all these points that Mr. Merz made, what is the foreign ministry’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China stands for openness and cooperation, and stays committed to working with all parties to keep global industrial and supply chains stable and secure and inject more impetus and certainty into world economy. Between China and Germany and between China and Europe, there is a high degree of economic complementarity. Our industries are mutually embedded and our practical cooperation is mutually beneficial. It is hoped that Germany and the EU will stay objective and rational, and work in the same direction with China, so that we can be each other’s trustworthy and predictable partners, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, keep the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded, and provide more certainty for cooperation between our business communities. AFP: French football star Kylian Mbappé apologized on Tuesday. He said his comments were “ill-judged,” and he now understands that “it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.” What is the foreign ministry think of his apology? (Similar question from Reuters) Guo Jiakun: We take seriously the apology he has made. China-Arab TV: On October 27 local time, Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have hit Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry building, airport and oil refinery in the capital with ballistic missiles and drones. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China is deeply concerned over the continued tensions in the region. We oppose attacks against civilian airports and other civilian facilities, and call on relevant parties to resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation and restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East at an early date.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 27, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
CCTV: Themed on “Justice and Peace for All Humanity,” the photo exhibition commemorating the 80th anniversary of the Tokyo Trials was held at the UN headquarters yesterday, with the participation of diplomats from various countries, officials from different international organizations and people of various sectors. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The Tokyo Trials hold great historical significance and relevance. This photo exhibition brings together a large number of photographs and archives of the Tokyo Trials depicting the true history of Japan’s militarist aggression and the wartime crimes to the international community. The United Nations was born out of humanity’s reflection on the devastation of war, therefore it fully serves the international community’s common pursuit of remembering history and cherishing peace to hold the exhibition in the UN. The Tokyo Trials constitute a historic trial in which peace subdued violence and justice prevailed over evil. The Trials are an integral part of the postwar international order. Recognizing and accepting the judgement of the Tokyo Trials is the prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community. Eighty years on, however, it is alarming that Japan’s right-wing forces still defy the historic verdict of the Tokyo Trials and try every possible means to deny and whitewash the crimes of aggression, promote a distorted view of history, and brazenly worship war criminals as “gods.” The international community should jointly push back against these trends. The lessons of history are still fresh in memory. Anyone who undermines peace and challenges righteousness and conscience is bound to be brought once again before the court of history and justice. As an important force in the World Anti-Fascist War, China stands ready to work with all peace-loving nations and peoples around the world to carry forward the belief in the rule of law and peace, firmly safeguard the truth of history, uphold the postwar international order, and defend international fairness and justice. AFP: French football star Kylian Mbappé was dropped today by a few major brands in China, after a video circulated online in which he apparently joked about China. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this incident. Guo Jiakun: We noted relevant reports. Any rhetoric or action that hurts the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be rejected across the sectors in China. Xinhua News Agency: We have noted a security alert issued by the Chinese embassy in the UK advising Chinese citizens to be aware of recent practices in UK border checks. Could you offer more information on this? Guo Jiakun: Recently, the Chinese Foreign Ministry and the Chinese embassy in the UK have received multiple reports of Chinese citizens being held and examined for extended hours by the UK police when entering and exiting the country, with their electronic devices including mobile phones seized. The Chinese side strongly deplores and is gravely concerned about the UK police’s arbitrary and excessive law enforcement actions. We have lodged serious démarches with the UK and will take all necessary measures to keep Chinese citizens safe and protect their legitimate and lawful rights and interests. We would like to remind Chinese citizens planning to travel to the UK to read carefully the embassy’s alert to avoid any inconvenience or loss. The Paper: The situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region has been evolving rapidly. The conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea remains highly intense. And there are reports suggesting that the United States and Israel might resume military operations against Iran. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China closely follows the developments in the Middle East, the Gulf region, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa, and expresses deep concerns over the protracted conflicts and their spillover effects. We call on relevant parties to resolve their disputes through dialogue and negotiation and realize lasting ceasefire and cessation of hostilities at an early date. China is committed to promoting peace talks. Our special envoys will soon travel to regional countries to strengthen communication with the relevant parties and promote engagement, dialogue and deescalation to prevent the worsening of the situation. Guided by the initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on promoting peace and security in the Middle East, China will work together with the international community to make unremitting efforts for the early realization of peace and stability in relevant regions. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed on Monday that Brazil’s elections were rigged after incumbent Lula’s win. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on what Trump said. Guo Jiakun: We respect the independent choice of the Brazilian people. Bloomberg: The European Union is planning potential trade measures that could be proposed early next year to cut imports of chemicals, furniture and machinery from China, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on this? Guo Jiakun: As far as China is concerned, the relationship with the EU is essentially a partnership, and the economic and trade ties are mutually beneficial. The success of the recent second meeting of the China-EU Trade and Investment Consultation fully proves that the two sides can properly handle differences in economy and trade through dialogue and consultation. It is in the interest of both sides to step up dialogue and consultation and deepen economic and trade cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, which is also the shared expectation of the business community and people of both sides. It is hoped that the EU will abide by the principles of market economy and fair competition, avoid abusing trade remedies, and take concrete actions to promote the steady and sound development of China-EU relations.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 26, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Iceland Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir will visit China from October 26 to 31. CCTV: China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an). How does China see the role of AI capacity-building in global governance? Guo Jiakun: Artificial intelligence is an emerging field in global governance, and a litmus test for the effectiveness of the global governance system. The global governance system would not become more just and equitable without the collective capacity enhancement of the Global South, and requires concrete efforts to strengthen the representation and voice of developing countries. China advocates for respecting the digital sovereignty of all countries. We believe that every country has the right to possess the foundational capabilities for independent AI development, and to seek a development path suited to its national conditions and practical needs, one that enables AI to be applied in real-world scenarios, address real problems, and generate sustained value. As a responsible major country, China remains committed to providing global public goods in the field of AI. In 2024, China promoted the adoption of a UN General Assembly resolution on enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence, established the Group of Friends for International Cooperation on AI Capacity-Building, and released the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All. Over the past two years, China has taken major steps and practical measures to honor its commitment in advancing the above-mentioned initiative. Recently, at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, which systematically reviews the cooperation outcomes, practical experience and specific cases since the Action Plan was launched two years ago. The report identifies access to technology as the starting point and independent development as the goal, stresses the importance of demand-driven approaches, joint consultation and co-development for project delivery, and calls for promoting openness and open source and advancing AI models, data, and talent in a coordinated manner. Looking ahead, we welcome more countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, to explore more pathways for international cooperation on AI capacity-building, and to promote global AI development for good and for all with concrete actions. Brasil de Fato: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has just won the reelection. Does the Chinese foreign ministry have a comment or message regarding the outcome of this election and the prospect of China-Brazil relations on Lula’s next term? (Similar question from UOL of Brazil) Guo Jiakun: China takes note of the announcement by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court of President Lula’s runoff victory and extends congratulations on that. China stands ready to work with Brazil to advance the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future. TV Asahi: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda just passed away. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: We express deep condolences and grief over former Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda’s passing and heartfelt sympathies to his family. Mr. Yasuo Fukuda is an old friend of the Chinese people, who actively contributed to the improvement and development of China-Japan relations. He has long been committed to the friendship between our two countries, and held a correct view of history. During his tenure as prime minister, China and Japan signed the fourth political document. After leaving office, he visited the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre. What’s more, he served for many years as Chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in facilitating exchanges and cooperation in Asia. Mr. Yasuo Fukuda once noted that the four political documents between China and Japan stipulated the principles governing bilateral relations, which we must bear in mind and never deviate from. Those firm and important remarks reflected the honor and responsibility of Japan’s statesman of the older generation and should evoke self-reflection and soul-searching among those currently running the Japanese government. AFP: Just following up on Brazil, Bolsonaro has called for those election results to be annulled. Does China have a comment on that? Guo Jiakun: China respects the choice of the Brazilian people. People’s Daily: On October 23, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi announced at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an) that China would issue a Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. Could you offer more information? Guo Jiakun: Outer space is the common frontier of all humanity and space exploration is humanity’s common endeavor. As announced by Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China has issued its Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. This is a major step by China to deliver on the four major global initiatives and advance efforts in building a community with a shared future for humanity in outer space. The position paper takes the common values of humanity as the fundamental guidance and advocates that the development and security, as well as the stability and sustainability of outer space, should be pursued in a balanced way. It proposes that we should commit to openness and shared benefit, abide by the international rule of law, respect the rights of all States, advance innovation and development, safeguard common security, prevent armed conflicts, reduce misunderstanding and misperception, regulate commercial space activity, deepen international cooperation, and promote global governance. The position paper outlines constructive approaches to address issues of common concern including development, security and governance in outer space, and provides a blueprint for relevant discussions and formulation of rules by the international community. China will continue working together with all parties in an open and constructive spirit to ensure that the outcomes of space development better benefit all humanity. China Daily: To follow up on Icelandic Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir’s upcoming visit you just announced, how does China see the current state of China-Iceland relations? What are your expectations for the visit? Guo Jiakun: We welcome Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir to visit China. China-Iceland relations have enjoyed sound momentum of growth in recent years. In 2025, when President Tómasdóttir was in China for the Global Leaders’ Meeting on Women, President Xi met with her and they reached important common understandings on deepening cooperation in such areas as economy and trade, geothermal energy, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges. As we mark the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Iceland this year, the Chinese side looks forward to in-depth exchanges with the Icelandic side on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest to further enhance trust, advance cooperation and renew our friendship. Yonhap News Agency: General Secretary of the Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK) and President of the State Affairs of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Kim Jong Un visited Dandong, China last week. Was the visit proposed by China or the DPRK? Can you share more information on this visit? Guo Jiakun: On October 24, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) Wang Huning accompanied General Secretary of the WPK and President of the State Affairs of the DPRK Kim Jong Un on a visit to Dandong. Wang Huning conveyed General Secretary of the Central Committee of the CPC and President Xi Jinping’s cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim Jong Un. China released a readout, which you may refer to. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors. It is an unswerving strategic policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to maintain, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. The sound and steady development of the China-DPRK traditional friendly cooperative ties is in the interest of both peoples and conducive to regional peace, stability, development and prosperity. China stands ready to work with the DPRK to deliver on the important common understandings of the two heads of state and further advance bilateral ties. Reuters: Regarding the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting Plus that will be held from this Wednesday in Manila, will China be participating in that meeting? Whether it’s sending high-level officials or delegation? Guo Jiakun: The ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus is meant to play a positive role in enabling regional countries to step up dialogue, increase trust and promote cooperation. We oppose attempts by anyone to use this platform to seek selfish gains, hijack ASEAN and create trouble. AFP: The United States last week designated the Confucius Institute Cultural Centers on American universities and campuses as a threat to U.S. national security. Would China like to comment? Guo Jiakun: We reject vilification and smears against Confucius Institute. Educational exchange and cooperation between China and the U.S. help enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of the two countries. They are desired by both sides and benefit both sides and should not be held back or disrupted. Beijing Youth Daily: Yesterday, the 25th of October, is the eighth Anti-Sanctions Day designated by the Southern African Development Community. Zimbabwe recently held commemorative events and called for the immediate removal of the illegal sanctions imposed by Western countries. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: China supports Zimbabwe in commemorating the Anti-Sanctions Day. The illegal sanctions imposed by certain Western countries on Zimbabwe have lasted for over 20 years. The practice is a typical example of hegemonism. It seriously violates Zimbabwe’s national sovereignty, undermines Zimbabwean people’s right to development, and hurts international fairness and justice. China has supported the just aspiration of Zimbabwe and other African friends in various ways for eight consecutive years. China solemnly calls on certain Western countries to immediately remove the illegal sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe, and take responsible and concrete actions to develop the economy and improve people’s livelihoods there. China will work with African countries and the rest of the world to safeguard international fairness and justice, and support Zimbabwe in defending independence and sovereignty as well as achieving development and revitalization. AFP: Serbia’s student-led movement won parliamentary elections on Sunday, ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic’s party. I was wondering if China would comment on the fact that Vucic said that the student movement was carried out with direct support from various European countries and the U.S. deep state. Guo Jiakun: China upholds the principle of non-interference in internal affairs and respects the independent choice of the people of other countries. We attach great importance to China-Serbia relations and stand ready to work with Serbia’s new government to carry forward our traditional friendship, consolidate political mutual trust and expand practical cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, so as to maintain the steady and sustained growth of bilateral ties. Bloomberg: India has held the Chinese military responsible for disturbing the peace on the border amid reports of fresh confrontation. A spokesman from India’s ministry of external affairs said this happens when Chinese forces diverge from established patterns. Does the foreign ministry have any comment? Guo Jiakun: China strictly abides by the relevant agreements and common understandings reached between the two countries, and conducts normal border patrol and control activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and stability in the border areas. China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels. We hope that India will work with China in the same direction by jointly implementing the common understandings reached between the two sides and maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas with concrete actions.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 23, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier will pay a state visit to China from October 27 to 31. Xinhua News Agency: On German President Steinmeier’s visit to China that you just announced, could you share the program? How does China see the current state of relations with Germany? What are your expectations for the visit? Mao Ning: President Steinmeier will visit China again after nearly eight years. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with him and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him to exchange views on bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest. Besides Beijing, President Steinmeier will also visit Anhui Province. The sound and steady growth of the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Germany, the world’s second and third largest economies, not only serves the interests of both countries, but is also what Europe and the world hope to see. The past 54 years since diplomatic ties were established have shown that mutual respect and mutual trust are the bedrock for a stable relationship and mutual benefit the key to success in bilateral cooperation. Our two countries have built strategic consensus through close collaboration and achieved shared prosperity in practical cooperation, delivering tangible benefits to both peoples. President Steinmeier, an old friend of the Chinese people, has actively contributed to the development of China-Germany relations. We hope to work with the German side to take this visit as an opportunity to cement mutual trust, deepen cooperation and seek joint innovation, so as to make greater progress in bilateral relations, contribute to steady and sustained growth of China-Europe relations, and bring fresh energy to the world. CCTV: October 25 will mark the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the lawful seat of the People’s Republic of China in the United Nations. How does China see its relationship with the UN over the past 55 years, and how will it enhance its cooperation with the organization in the future? Mao Ning: On October 25, 1971, the UN General Assembly adopted at its 26th session Resolution 2758 with an overwhelming majority, deciding to restore all rights of the People’s Republic of China in the United Nations. This marked the return of the Chinese people, one-fourth of the world’s population, back to the UN stage, which is of great significance and far-reaching impact for China, the wider world and the United Nations itself. The Chinese people shall always remember the invaluable support and help we received from friendly countries and individuals. Over the past 55 years, China has always been a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development, and a guardian of the international order. We firmly support the UN in playing a central role in international affairs, actively participate in the work of the UN in various fields, and faithfully fulfill our duties as a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Through the UN, we work to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with other countries, advocate for common security, promote shared development, foster dialogue among civilizations, and advance the reform and improvement of global governance. Standing at this new starting point of history, China will continue to shoulder its responsibility as a major country, further deepen cooperation with the UN across the board, jointly tackle global challenges, and build a community with a shared future for humanity. Reuters: The U.S. Treasury has proposed to add biotechnology as a new “prohibited technology” under the U.S. Outbound Investment Security Program. This could restrict American investments in Chinese biotechnology companies. How does the ministry view this measure? Mao Ning: It serves no one’s interest to take discriminatory measures targeting specific countries or putting restrictions on economic, trade and investment activities based on overstretching the concept of national security. The U.S. should abide by the principles of market economy, stop disrupting normal business cooperation, and help keep global industrial and supply chains stable through concrete actions. China will closely follow relevant developments and take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on the 7.6 Magnitude Earthquake in Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Q: It’s reported that a 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama on October 10, followed by over 100 aftershocks. What is China’s comment? A: China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there is no report of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and promptly provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need. We remind Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.
